
## Olorofim · a new target for mould disease

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
**Mechanism**

- First member of the **orotomide** class (F901318). Inhibits **fungal dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH)**,
  the rate-limiting enzyme of **de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis** [@oliver2016f901318].
- Fungi depend on *de novo* synthesis; the **human DHODH is not meaningfully inhibited**, which limits
  on-target toxicity.
- **Fungicidal against moulds**; the deficit is structural, not incidental — no activity against **yeasts**
  (*Candida*, *Cryptococcus*) or **Mucorales**.

**Microbiology**

- Potent against *Aspergillus* spp. **irrespective of azole susceptibility**, including TR~34~/L98H isolates.
- Active against the organisms with no other options: ***Lomentospora prolificans***, ***Scedosporium*** spp.,
  *Coccidioides* spp., *Microascus*/*Scopulariopsis*, and other rare moulds; variable against *Fusarium*
  [@olorofim2021potency; @jenks2024olorofim].
- **No *in vitro* cross-resistance** with any licensed class.
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
| PK parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Formulation | **Oral only** (IV in development) |
| Oral bioavailability | ~**45%** |
| Solubility / binding | Poorly water-soluble; **highly protein bound** |
| Metabolism | Multiple CYP450 enzymes **including CYP3A4** |
| Perpetrator risk | **Weak CYP3A4 inhibitor** — low interaction potential |
| PD index | AUC/MEC; target **C~min~ ≥0.1–0.2 mg/L** |

**Dosing as studied:** initially weight-based (180–300 mg loading, then 120–240 mg/day in divided doses);
simplified from patient 59 onward to **150 mg twice on day 1, then 90 mg twice daily**.

::: {.pearl}
Population PK modelling showed that **weight-based dosing and routine TDM could be dropped** without
materially changing plasma concentrations — C~min~ consistently exceeded the PD target in both the TDM and
fixed-dose groups.
:::
:::
:::

## Olorofim · FORMULA-OLS phase 2b {.smaller}

**Design.** Single-arm, open-label, 22 centres in 11 countries. Patients ≥16 years with proven IFD or probable
invasive pulmonary aspergillosis and **few or no treatment options**: 203 treated, **202 with
committee-adjudicated IFD** [@maertens2025formulaols].

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Population** — this is a salvage cohort, not a first-line trial

- *Aspergillus* spp. 101 (**22 azole-resistant**), *Coccidioides* spp. 41,
  *L. prolificans* 26, *Scedosporium* spp. 22, other 12
- Reason for enrolment: **failure of available therapy 54%**, resistance to all licensed agents 25%,
  intolerance 14%
- 95% had received prior antifungal therapy (median 2 agents); median **75 days** from diagnosis to first dose
- Sites: lung/sinonasal 62%, **CNS 24%**, bone/joint 17%, disseminated 25%
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Outcomes**

| Endpoint | Day 42 | Day 84 |
|---|---|---|
| Global response success | **28.7%** (95% CI 22.6–35.5) | 27.2% (21.2–33.9) |
| Success with stable disease counted as success | **75.2%** (68.7–81.0) | 63.4% (56.3–70.0) |
| Clinical response | 59.9% (52.8–66.7) | 54.0% (46.8–61.0) |
| All-cause mortality | **11.9%** (7.8–17.2) | 16.3% (11.5–22.2) |

By pathogen (global response, day 42): *L. prolificans* **42.3%**, *Scedosporium* 36.4%, *Aspergillus* 34.7%,
other susceptible moulds 33.3%, **Coccidioides 0%**.
:::
:::

::: {.keypoint}
**Interpreting a 28.7% global response.** The composite requires improvement in clinical, radiological **and**
mycological components; stable disease counts as failure. In extrapulmonary coccidioidomycosis mycological
eradication is not achievable at all — yet **75.6%** of those 41 patients had a complete or partial
**clinical** response. All-cause mortality of 11.9% at day 42 in a cohort that had already failed everything
is the number that matters most.
:::

## Olorofim · safety, interactions and place in therapy

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
**Safety**

- **Hepatic.** Medically significant liver-enzyme elevations at least possibly attributable to olorofim in
  **20/203 (10%)**, adjudicated by an independent hepatic advisory committee. Managed by **dose reduction or
  pause in 14 (7%)** and **permanent discontinuation in 6 (3%)**. All events resolved; **no liver failure and
  no hepatic deaths**. Events clustered in the first 12 weeks.
- **Gastrointestinal intolerance** in 10%, predominantly mild or moderate and self-limiting.
- Adverse events of special interest also included neurological symptoms, hypotension, vertigo, syncope and
  dry eye.
- Well tolerated with **>2 years** of continuous therapy in the extended-treatment phase (114 patients,
  mean 361 days).
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Interactions**

- Fluconazole (moderate CYP3A4/2C9 inhibitor) increased olorofim **AUC~0–72~ by 1.5–1.6×** without a
  significant C~max~ change.
- As a **weak CYP3A4 inhibitor**, olorofim required calcineurin-inhibitor dose reduction within 14 days in
  **9/18 (50%)** patients on ciclosporin (median 50% reduction) and **8/46 (17%)** on tacrolimus (median 29%).
  **No change** was needed for tyrosine kinase inhibitors or venetoclax.

**Resistance**

- The only mechanism described so far is **target alteration**: substitutions at the **G119** codon of the
  DHODH gene (*pyrE*) — G119A, G119V, G119S, G119C confirmed in recombinant enzyme — plus one H116P isolate.

::: {.keypoint}
**Place in therapy.** An oral, fungicidal, mechanistically novel agent for azole-resistant aspergillosis,
*L. prolificans*, *Scedosporium* and refractory coccidioidomycosis — with CNS activity. The phase 3 **OASIS**
trial compares oral olorofim with liposomal amphotericin B followed by standard of care in invasive
aspergillosis, with day-42 all-cause mortality as the primary endpoint.
:::
:::
:::
